front: What are the regulation field dimensions (length and width), and how long is each end zone? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 1 – Definitions and Markings
back: The field of play is 110 yards (100 metres) long by 65 yards (60 metres) wide, with an end zone 20 yards (18.28 metres) long at each end.

front: Which lines define the end zone, and is the goal line part of it? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 1 – Definitions and Markings
back: The end zone is bounded by the goal line, end zone sidelines, and dead line; the goal line is part of the end zone.

front: What is the dead line, and where is it located relative to each goal line? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 1 – Definitions and Markings
back: The dead line is the line 20 yards (18.28 metres) behind each goal line and parallel to it.

front: What specifically counts as the bounds of the playing field, and are these boundary lines in or out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 2 – Boundaries
back: The bounds are defined as the inside of the sidelines, end zone sidelines, and dead lines; these boundary lines are out of bounds.

front: From what edge are all field measurements taken? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 3 – Field Dimension Measurements
back: All measurements are taken from the inside edge of any boundary line.

front: How are the distance lines marked across the field? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 4 – Distance Lines
back: The field of play is marked every 5 yards (metres) by lines parallel to the goal line and extending completely across the field between the sidelines.

front: Which yard lines must be double thickness (or double lines), and at what distances? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 5 – Special Lines
back: The 35 and 45 yard (30 and 40 metre) lines must be of double thickness or double lines.

front: Where are hash marks placed and how are they spaced? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 6 – Hash Marks
back: Twenty-four yards (22 metres) from each sideline, each 5 yard (metre) stripe has a short cross stripe parallel to the sideline (hash marks).

front: What is recommended regarding markers near each distance line? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 7 – Distance Markers
back: It is recommended that markers be placed opposite each 5 yard (metre) line indicating the distance of each line from the goal line toward the centre of the field.

front: What type of markers may be used at the end zone boundary intersections, and are they inbounds? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 8 – End Zone Markings
back: Only flexible markers may be used to mark the four intersections of the goal lines and sidelines and the four intersections of the dead line and the end zone sidelines; they must be placed at the intersection of the lines and are considered inbounds.

front: Under what condition must rigid objects at the end zone intersections be removed? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 8 – End Zone Markings
back: If any rigid object is present, it shall be removed before the start of the game.

front: What are the size and construction requirements for the flexible end zone pylon markers? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 8 – End Zone Markings
back: Markers must be soft, flexible, four-sided pylons, 4” x 4” (10 cm x 10 cm), with an overall height of 18 inches (46 cm) and may include a two inch (5 cm) space between the bottom of the pylon and the ground; they must be orange or red in colour.

front: How far apart are the vertical goal posts, and where are they centered? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: The two vertical goal posts are 18 feet 6 inches (5.64 metres) apart and centred on the goal line.

front: How high is the crossbar’s upper edge above the ground? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: The crossbar joining the goal posts has its upper edge 10 feet (3.05 metres) above the ground.

front: What minimum height above the ground are goal posts required to be? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: For safety, the goal posts must be at least 20 feet (6.1 metres) above the ground level.

front: Where can the base of the goal post be located relative to the goal line? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: The base of the goal post can be up to 110 inches (279.4 cm) behind the goal line.

front: Who is responsible for providing goal post padding, and what must be true for safety? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: The home team is responsible for providing the padding; all goal posts must be properly padded with goal post pads meeting manufacturer’s specifications.

front: In a neutral field, who decides which team provides the goal post padding? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: On a neutral field, the participating teams decide which team is responsible for padding the goal posts.

front: Are goal posts on the goal line considered part of the end zone? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: Yes—goal posts on the goal line are considered to be part of the end zone.

front: Under what condition may a field use non-regulation boundary placement, and what spacing rule must be followed? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 10 – Non-Regulation Fields
back: When the length or width is less than regulation due to running tracks or other obstructions, clear boundary lines must be provided at least 1 foot (0.3 metres) inside the track or obstruction.

front: If an end zone is shorter than required and enclosed by a track, how must the dead line and end zone sideline be marked? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 10 – Non-Regulation Fields
back: The dead line and end zone sideline must be clearly marked at least 1 foot (0.3 metres) inside the curb.

front: What qualifies as a “play” under this rule? Rule 1 | Section 1: The Field | Article 11 – Play
back: A play is any legally run scrimmage play (run, pass, kick), a convert attempt, or a kick-off, during both regulation time and overtime.

front: What is the required construction and inflation pressure range for the four-panel ball? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: The ball is a four-panel ball made of pebbled grain leather, enclosing a rubber bladder, tightly inflated to not less than 12 1/2 lbs (85 kPa) and not more than 13 1/2 lbs (95 kPa).

front: What shape and axis dimensions are required for the ball’s prolate spheroid? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: It shall be in the shape of a prolate spheroid. The circumference of the long axis shall be from 27 3/4 to 28 1/2 inches (700–725 mm); the circumference of the short axis from 20 3/4 to 21 3/8 inches (525–540 mm). The length of the long axis shall be from 10 7/8 to 11 7/16 inches (275–290 mm).

front: What weight range must the ball meet? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: The ball must weigh from 14 to 15 ounces (400–425 grams).

front: Who provides the ball(s) for the game, and whose decision determines whether the ball is suitable? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: The Home Team shall provide a league approved ball or balls. The decision of the Referee is final as to the suitability of the ball.

front: Under what condition must the ball be a natural tan color, and under what condition must its color be chosen for visibility? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 2 – Day and Night Games
back: For day games, the ball shall be of a natural tan in colour. For night games, the ball must be of such colour as will make it clearly visible.

front: What uniform-matching restriction applies to the ball’s color in both day and night games? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 2 – Day and Night Games
back: In both day and night games, the colour of the ball shall, in no way, closely blend with the colour of the uniforms of the competing teams.

front: On wet days, how many balls should be available and how may they be used? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 3 – Wet Day Procedure
back: On wet days, it is recommended that at least three balls be available, which may be changed at the discretion of the Referee.

front: What assistance is suggested on wet days to keep balls clean and dry? Rule 1 | Section 2: The Ball | Article 3 – Wet Day Procedure
back: It is suggested that “ball persons” be used, one on either side of the field, to keep the balls as clean and dry as possible.

front: How many total minutes of actual playing time are played in a standard game, and how is it divided into periods? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 1 – Length of Game
back: The game consists of 60 minutes of actual playing time, divided into 4 periods of 15 minutes each.

front: For players at the High School level or equivalent and below, how long is actual playing time and how is it divided? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 1 – Length of Game
back: 48 minutes of actual playing time, divided into 4 periods of 12 minutes each.

front: At the start of the game, what procedure determines which captain has first choice for kickoff/receiving/defending an end? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 2 – Choice of Kick Off, Receiving Kick Off, or End of Field
back: The captain of the visiting team, or the team winning the coin toss, declares whether to have first choice at the start of the first or second half.

front: When a team captain has first choice at the start of the first half, what options are available, and how does the other captain’s choice differ? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 2 – Choice of Kick Off, Receiving Kick Off, or End of Field
back: First choice includes: (1) Kicking Off, (2) Receiving the kick off, or (3) Defending an end of the field. The other captain then has the option of the remaining 1 or 2 choices.

front: How does the choice procedure change at the start of the 3rd period? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 2 – Choice of Kick Off, Receiving Kick Off, or End of Field
back: At the start of the 3rd period, the procedure shall be reversed.

front: After a touchdown, who has the choice, and what are the two options? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 2 – Choice of Kick Off, Receiving Kick Off, or End of Field
back: After a touchdown, the captain of the team scored against has the choice of kicking off, or receiving the kick off.

front: When do teams change ends of the field? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 3 – Change of End
back: At the end of the 1st and 3rd periods, the teams shall change ends.

front: How is the ball put into play at the start of the 2nd and 4th periods relative to when it became dead at the end of the previous period? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 3 – Change of End
back: At the start of the 2nd and 4th periods, the ball is put into play at a point corresponding exactly to where the ball became dead at the opposite end, and in exactly the same manner as if play had not been interrupted by the end of the previous period.

front: How long is the rest period at halftime, and what flexibility is allowed? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 4 – Half Time
back: At the end of the 2nd period, a 20-minute rest period shall be allowed, or such other rest period as the league shall decide.

front: What penalty applies if a team is late appearing on the field at the start of the 1st or 3rd period? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 5 – Late Start
back: Penalty – L10. No option.

front: Who decides the procedure to break a tie after the end of the 4th period, and what must be communicated in advance? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: The governing football association decides the procedure, considering athlete safety as prime importance. Any procedures must be communicated in writing to both teams and to the Referee prior to the game.

front: If no tie-breaking regulations have been prepared, what are the officials required to do immediately after the fourth quarter? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: Immediately after the conclusion of the fourth quarter, officials instruct both teams to retire to their respective team areas. Officials then assemble at center field and review the tie-breaking procedure.

front: In the no-prepared-regulations tie procedure, what does the coin toss determine first extra period option-wise? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: Officials escort captains to the center of the field for the coin toss. The toss winner chooses one of: (1) Offense or defense (offense at the opponent’s 35-yard line to start), or (2) Which end of the field shall be used for the overtime period. The toss loser exercises the remaining option for the first extra period.

front: Under the no-prepared-regulations overtime rules, how is possession placed and where can teams snap to put the ball in play? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: An extra period provides each team the opportunity to put the ball in play by a snap, on or between the hash marks of the opponent’s 35-yard line (except if Team B scores during a Team A possession).

front: In an extra period, when does the ball remain alive after a change of team possession? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: The ball remains alive after a change of team possession until it is declared dead.

front: How is the winner determined during overtime, and what changes if the score remains tied after three extra periods? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: The team scoring the greater number of points during an extra period wins. If still tied after three extra periods, any subsequent touchdown must be followed by a two-point conversion.

front: Are team time-outs allowed during overtime play under the no-prepared-regulations procedure? Rule 1 | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: No—there shall be no team time-outs during overtime play.

front: How many players may each team have on the field at any one time? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 1 – Teams
back: Each team consists of 12 players on the field at any one time.

front: In Approved Rulings in the Case Book, how are the teams identified when a team puts the ball into play? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 2 – Team Designation
back: The team which puts the ball into play shall be identified as Team A, and the other team as Team B.

front: What requirement must each team meet regarding the captain, and how is the captain identified to officials? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: At all times, each team shall have on the field a player designated as captain, and so identified to the officials.

front: Who is allowed to communicate between the team and the officials, and what limitation applies to that communication? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: The captain is the sole communicator between the team and the officials (through the Referee), and no prolonged argument is to be allowed; the Referee’s decision cannot be disputed.

front: What penalty applies if a player (or anyone on the bench) comments to benefit the officials? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: Commenting by a player, or any occupant of the bench, for the supposed benefit of the officials shall be penalized: Penalty L10. No option.

front: When the Referee informs a captain of a choice (e.g., kickoff start of a half or after a touchdown/field goal), what happens after the choice is communicated or made? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: After the choice on a kick off has been communicated to the opponents by the Referee, the choice may not be revoked. After the choice of penalty or option has been made, the choice may not be revoked.

front: Under what condition may the Referee decline a request for a measurement about whether a first down was made? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: The Referee may decline a request for a measurement if satisfied beyond all reasonable doubt that a first down has or has not been made.

front: When distance chains are called to determine whether a first down was made, who is permitted to be near the measurement? Rule 1 | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: Only the on-field captain of each team shall be permitted in the vicinity of the measurement.

front: When does the game clock/time start according to the timing rules after a kickoff? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 1 – Time Starts
back: Time shall start on the signal of the Referee when, following a kick off, the ball touches or is touched by a player of either team in bounds.

front: Under what condition does time start immediately due to an improper play timing cue (e.g., after a time count foul or timeout for crowd noise)? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 1 – Time Starts
back: Time shall start when the ball is snapped after a “time count” foul, or after a timeout due to the noise of the crowd.

front: After the 3-minute warning, what situations can cause the ball to be snapped (and time to start) immediately? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 1 – Time Starts
back: Time starts when the ball is snapped following (1) an incomplete forward pass or a ball carried out of bounds after the 3-minute warning in any half; (2) a play in which possession changes after the 3-minute warning (including after a score of 1 or 3 points when the ball is put into play by a scrimmage); (3) a play immediately following a kick off, a kick from scrimmage, a return kick, or an open field kick after the 3-minute warning; or (4) after penalty application for a foul that occurs after the 3-minute warning (with the non-offending team allowed to decline the penalty and resume as though no foul occurred).

front: What events cause time to stop on the signal of a field official? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 2 – Time Stops
back: Time shall stop when: (a) a score has been made and throughout any convert attempt; (b) a live ball goes out of bounds; (c) a forward pass is incomplete; (d) penalty application is required; (e) three or more players from either team substitute at the same time; (f) player injury occurs (time stops after the ball is dead and the injured player must be replaced); (g) time expires at the end of a period; (h) the ball becomes dead after the three-minute warning signal in any half; (i) any field official recognizes a request for a time out; (j) the Referee suspends play (defective equipment, measurements, etc.); (k) a play ends in which Team B has gained possession at some point during the play; or (l) termination of all kick plays occurs.

front: If the ball becomes dead with only a short time remaining in a period, what does the team in possession get? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 3 – End of Period
back: The team in possession is entitled to one complete play, even though that play may extend beyond the normal termination of that period.

front: When is a period extended after a legally scored touchdown on the last play? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 3 – End of Period
back: If the last play is a legally scored touchdown, the period will be extended for the convert attempt following the touchdown, ending when the ball is declared dead on the convert without a foul; if a foul occurs, see Rule 1, Section 5, Article 6.

front: How many time outs does each team have per half, and how long is each time out? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 4 – Time Out
back: Each team is entitled to two time outs in each half, and each time out is 1 minute long.

front: From when can a team request a time out, and when may a team no longer keep players near the bench? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 4 – Time Out
back: A time out may be requested from the time the ball becomes dead until it is put into play. After a time out (and any conference with the coaches), Team A players must not remain in close proximity to their bench; they must return to their huddle (or move clearly away from the bench area if not using a huddle) or be penalized for illegal procedure.

front: Under what score difference and timing condition does the mercy rule apply, and what exceptions keep the clock from running? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 5 – Mercy Rule
back: Any time after the first half, if the difference in score becomes 35 points or more, the clock will be running time for the remainder of the game, except for injuries, scores, timeouts, or any reason the Referee deems necessary to stop the clock. When the clock is stopped, it will re-start based on rule 1-5-1.

front: Does the mercy rule apply at U Sport and CJFL levels? Rule 1 | Section 5: Timing | Article 5 – Mercy Rule
back: No. The mercy rule does not apply for U Sport and CJFL levels.

front: What does it mean for a player to be in possession of the ball? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 1 – Player Possession
back: A player is in possession when the ball is firmly held in the hand or hands, arm or arms, leg or legs, or under the body.

front: When players of opposite teams have possession at the same time, who does the ball belong to? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 2 – Disputed Possession
back: It belongs to the player who first gained possession and has not lost possession.

front: If players of opposite teams legally gain simultaneous possession, who gets possession? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 3 – Simultaneous Possession
back: It belongs to the team which last previously had possession.

front: If an eligible forward pass is caught simultaneously by receivers of both teams, who gets the ball? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 3 – Simultaneous Possession
back: The ball shall belong to Team A (Rule 6-4-6-c).

front: On a kickoff legally caught simultaneously by players of opposite teams, how do you decide possession based on whether the ball was touched before the simultaneous catch? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 3 – Simultaneous Possession
back:
- If caught before it has been touched by any other player after the kickoff: kickoff repeated at the previous line of kickoff.
- If caught after it has been legally touched by another player (or players): possession to the team which last touched it before the simultaneous possession.

front: In a scrimmage play, when does possession remain with Team A and when does it change to Team B? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team A is in possession until it loses possession (e.g., fumble, blocked kick). Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until either team gains possession, the ball is a «loose ball.»

front: On a forward pass, when is Team A in possession and when does Team B take possession? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team A is in possession until the pass is ruled incomplete, or the ball is intercepted by Team B. Team B is in possession when a B player intercepts the pass.

front: On a scrimmage kick, when does possession change and what is the ball called before possession changes? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team A is in possession until the ball is kicked. Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team B or Team A gains possession, the ball is in neither team’s possession and is a ball «in flight.»

front: On a return kick, when is Team B in possession and what is the status of the ball before either team regains possession? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team B is in possession until the B player has kicked the ball, which is then «in flight» until either Team A or Team B regains possession.

front: During a kickoff, which team is in possession before the kick, and when does possession change? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Neither team is in possession prior to the kick off. Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team B or Team A gains possession, the ball is in neither team’s possession and is a ball «in flight.»

front: If a kicked ball other than a kickoff is legally touched by a player, how is that touching treated when determining possession for penalty applications? Rule 1 | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Such touching shall be deemed to be possession when penalty applications are involved, with determination of before loose ball/ball in flight and after change of possession.

front: When is the ball considered in play? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: The ball is in play when it has been put into play by a kick off or scrimmage until a field official stops play by sounding the whistle.

front: What happens if the ball strikes an official who is not out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: The ball remains in play when it strikes an official who is not out of bounds, except on a forward pass.

front: Under what condition is a ball in play when it is on the ground? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: A ball is in play when it is on the ground not in possession of a player.

front: When is a ball held for a place kick still considered in play? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: A ball is in play when it is held in position by a player for the purpose of making a place kick, except on a kick off.

front: If a forward pass is intercepted in the end zone, what is the status of the ball? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: A forward pass intercepted by a player in their end zone results in the ball being in play.

front: Which kicking/passing scenarios keep the ball in play involving the goal post assembly? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: The ball is in play when a dribbled ball hits the goal post assembly; a kicked ball hits the goal post assembly after striking the ground, a player, or official, or after being kicked from the end zone; or a lateral pass hits the goal post assembly.

front: When may the play be stopped due to player injury and/or penalties? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: The play shall not be stopped because of player injury, or to impose a penalty until the ball is dead.

front: Is delay allowed for player injury, and who may authorize exceptions? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: No delay shall be allowed for player injury (or any other reason), except by permission of a field official.

front: What is the penalty for unauthorized delay due to injury or other reasons? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: Penalty for unauthorized delay is L10, no option.

front: What time out allowance does the Referee provide for medical attention or bleeding-related equipment, and are teams charged time outs? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: To avoid penalizing teams unduly, the Referee will call an official time out of no more than two (2) minutes for medical attention and/or care of equipment related to bleeding; neither Team is charged with a time out.

front: When does the ball become dead due to the end of play being signaled by officials? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: The ball becomes dead when a field official blows the whistle to end play (NOTE 4).

front: Under what conditions does the ball become dead when it goes beyond the field of play or related possession limits? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: The ball becomes dead when the ball, or a player with possession of the ball, goes out of bounds (NOTE 4).

front: What scoring event causes the ball to become dead? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: Any score is made.

front: When is a tackled/held ball carrier considered to have resulted in a dead ball? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: The ball becomes dead when the ball carrier is tackled, held and the forward progress has been halted (See Notes 1, 2, 3).

front: When does a forward pass cause the ball to become dead? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: A forward pass is declared incomplete, or it strikes a game official, the goal post assembly, downs box marker or distance chain rod.

front: Under what conditions related to possession prior to a kickoff does the ball become dead? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: It is in possession of a player lying on the ground or is being held by a player for a kick off, prior to the kick off.

front: If a kick hits the opponent’s goal post assembly in flight without touching the ground, player, or official, when is the play whistled dead and when does the ball remain alive on field goal/convert attempts? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: If the ball strikes the opponent’s goal post assembly in flight from a punt, return kick, place kick or kick off without touching the ground, a player or an official after being kicked, and the kick originated in the field of play, then the play shall be whistled dead. However, on a field goal or convert attempt, the ball will remain alive until the score is made or missed.

front: What part of a ball carrier touching the ground makes the ball dead, and at what point is it declared dead? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: Any part of a ball carrier, other than hands or feet, touches the ground—even without contact by an opponent. The ball shall be declared dead AT THE POINT WHERE IT WAS HELD when the ball carrier touched the ground. Exception: The ball is not dead when a player is holding the ball for a field goal or convert attempt.

front: If the ball carrier falls on a player who is on the ground, where is the ball declared dead? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: The ball shall be declared dead at that point, except if they are in the close line play area.

front: When does the ball become dead immediately regarding a ball carrier’s helmet? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: Immediately if ball carrier loses their helmet.

front: When does simulating or faking a slide cause the ball to become dead? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: A ball carrier begins, simulates, or fakes a foot-first slide.

front: When a ball carrier is tackled and driven back toward their own goal line, how is the forward point of the dead ball determined? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1 Note 1
back: It is assumed the ball carrier was attempting to advance, and only the opponent’s contact prevented the advance. Therefore, the most forward point of advance is considered to be the point where the ball became dead.

front: If the contacted ball carrier breaks the tackle, tries to advance, and retreats toward their own goal line, where is the dead-ball point determined? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1 Note 2
back: The point of advance where the ball becomes dead is considered as the point at which the ball carrier is subsequently held.

front: If a player is driven back into their end zone by contact but is not held, can they continue advancing, and what happens if the ball goes dead in possession in the end zone? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1 Note 3
back: If the player is contacted so the force drives them back into their end zone but they are not held, the player is still free to advance the ball. If the ball subsequently goes dead in their end zone, in the team’s possession, without having again left the end zone, the defending team shall be awarded 1 or 2 points, as applicable. If the ball is subsequently carried out of the end zone, the forward point of advance will be the point where the ball becomes dead.

front: When the whistle is blown inadvertently and a team is in possession, what two options does that team have? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1 Note 4
back: With a team in possession, the team in possession shall have the choice to: (i) cancel the current play and repeat it where it began (PLS or kick-off) OR (ii) have the play terminate at the PBH when the whistle was blown; downs continue if distance not gained.

front: If the whistle is blown inadvertently while a pass is in the air on a pass play, what is the repeat spot option? Rule 1 | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1 Note 4(1) Note
back: If in air on a pass play, repeat from PLS no option.

front: When is the ball considered to be in the End Zone (including cases where it is not fully on the ground)? Rule 1 | Section 9: End Zone | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is in the End Zone when any part of the ball is on, or behind, the goal line—even in the air.

front: Under what condition is the ball in the End Zone based on touching the goal line? Rule 1 | Section 9: End Zone | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is in the End Zone when any part of the ball touches the plane of the goal line.

front: Under what condition is the ball NOT in the End Zone? Rule 1 | Section 9: End Zone | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is not in the End Zone when the whole ball is completely ahead of the goal line, or the plane of the goal line.

front: When is the ball considered out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is out of bounds when it touches any boundary line, or the ground or any object on or beyond these lines, including an official, any player, or substitute.

front: Under what condition does a player in possession going out of bounds not make the ball out of bounds? Rule 1 | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 1 – Definition
back: It is only an out-of-bounds situation for the ball if the player touches any boundary line or the ground/objects beyond these lines—except when the ball carrier is fully in bounds and the only out-of-bounds touch is by a field official or another player who is out of bounds.

front: When the ball is carried out of bounds on the field of play, where does possession go (and what changes on third down)? Rule 1 | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 2 – Carried Out of Bounds
back: It belongs to the team carrying it out of bounds at the point where the ball crossed the line before it went out of bounds—except on third down when the required distance has not been gained.

front: What team gains possession when the ball is kicked out of bounds on the field of play? Rule 1 | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 3 – Kicked Out of Bounds
back: It belongs to the opposite team, subject to the option of penalty applicable on the play.

front: What happens when a player kicks the ball out of bounds in their own end zone? Rule 1 | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 3 – Kicked Out of Bounds
back: It results in a score of 1 or 2 points, unless the ball is in the end zone from a forward pass intercepted in the end zone, or as a result of a fumble into the end zone by an opponent.

front: When a forward pass is thrown out of bounds, who keeps possession (and what exception applies on third down)? Rule 1 | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 4 – Forward Pass Thrown Out of Bounds
back: Possession remains with the passing team, except on third down when the required distance has not been gained.

front: What equipment restrictions apply if a player’s gear could injure an opponent, and what action can the Referee take? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(a) – General
back: No player shall wear equipment of any kind which may injure the opponent. The Referee may remove from the game any player wearing equipment which, in the Referee’s opinion, endangers a participant.

front: Under what condition are team uniforms illegal, and what must be true about jersey numbers? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(b) – General
back: Teams must not wear uniforms that blend closely with the color of the ball. Uniforms must have numbers that are easy to identify.

front: What is mandatory protective equipment that all players must wear under this section? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(c) – Mandatory equipment
back: Knee protection; thigh guards; hip pads with tailbone protector; shoulder pads; mouthguard covering all upper jaw teeth; shoes meeting the specifications of Article 4 of this section (or acceptable lower-fixation alternatives noted). Also: items 1,2,3,4 and all Back Plates and Rib Protectors must be covered by pants or jersey except for the specified snap-in soft foam hip/tail pad system.

front: What limitations apply to knee protection, specifically regarding straps and closure types? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(c)1 – Knee protection
back: Knee protection must be either soft padding entirely captured within continuous material or designed for and insertable in football pants. Knee protection cannot include any strap featuring a buckle, Velcro, clip, or strap that could become unfastened during play.

front: When must Back Plates and Rib Protectors be covered by the pants or jersey, and what exception is allowed? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(c)7 – Coverage requirement
back: Items 1, 2, 3, 4 including all Back Plates and Rib Protectors must be covered by the pants or jersey, except for players wearing a snap-in soft foam hip and tail pad system.

front: What is illegal regarding adhesive material, grease, or slippery substances applied to a player? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(d) – Illegal substances
back: Adhesive material, grease, or any other slippery substance applied on a player’s person or clothing that affects the ball or an opponent is illegal.

front: What glove design is prohibited? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(e) – Gloves
back: Any gloves that have webbing between the digits are illegal.

front: When can a player change jersey numbers, and what must be reported if a sweater is torn? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(f) – Numbers
back: Players must conform to the numbers listed on the score sheet and must retain the same numbers throughout the game except when permission to change is given by the Referee. If a sweater is torn, the Referee shall allow reasonable time for a substitution, but any change in number must be reported to the scorer.

front: What is illegal about team jerseys under this rule? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1(g) – Illegal jerseys
back: It is illegal to tie or knot team jerseys.

front: For violations listed under Penalty a), b), f), or g), what is the consequence? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Penalty a/b/f/g
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the illegal equipment is replaced or the score sheet is corrected.

front: What is the yardage penalty and removal requirement for Penalty c violations? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Penalty c
back: Loss of 5 yards from the point where the ball would have been put into play, if no other foul had occurred (or added to the penalty for any other foul). The offending player shall be removed from the game until the illegal equipment is replaced; immediate substitution will be made but the game shall not be delayed. If more than 1 player offends on the same play, only 1 L5 is applied for that play (and subsequent plays are penalized similarly—L5 on each play where 1 or more players offend).

front: What is the consequence for Penalty d) and e) violations when more than one player offends on the same play? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Penalty d/e
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the illegal material, substance or gloves have been removed. Immediate substitution will be made but the game shall not be delayed. If more than one player offends on the same play, only 1 penalty L10 will be applied for that play; fouls on subsequent plays are penalized the same way—L10 on each play where 1 or more players offend.

front: What helmet and facemask requirement must be met before a player can wear them? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 2(a) – Helmets and facemasks
back: Only helmets and facemasks approved by the National Operating Committee on Safety in Athletic Equipment (NOCSAE) shall be worn by players.

front: When are visors legal, and are there any medical exceptions? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 2(b) – Visors
back: All visors must be clear, not tinted. No medical exceptions are allowed.

front: Under what condition must a player wear the helmet while the play is in progress? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 2(c) – Helmet during play
back: A player shall be required to wear the helmet while in bounds and shall not voluntarily remove it while the play is in progress.

front: If a player’s helmet involuntarily comes off during the play (except due to a foul), what must they do and for how long? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 2(e) – Helmet involuntarily comes off
back: They shall be required to leave the game for 3 plays.

front: What must a player do if they lose their helmet, and what is the penalty? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 2(f) – Helmet lost
back: The player must stop participating in the play. Penalty: L10 PBD or PBH.

front: How should contact be ruled if a player who has lost their helmet is hit? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 2(g) – Helmetless opponent
back: Hitting a player who has lost their helmet is to be ruled Unnecessary Roughness.

front: When is it illegal for a player to participate regarding mouthguards? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 3 – Mouthguard position
back: It shall be illegal for a player to participate in the game unless the mouthguard is being worn in the proper position by the player.

front: What are the consequences for mouthguard violations on the 1st infraction vs. 2nd and subsequent infractions? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 3 – Mouthguard penalties
back: 1st infraction: Referee only clearly warns the offending player that the mouthguard must be in proper position. 2nd & subsequent: L5 from the point where the ball would have been put in play if no foul had occurred; player removed until properly equipped; immediate substitution allowed.

front: What footwear types are acceptable for playing surfaces under Article 4? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 4 – Footwear accepted
back: A cleated shoe meeting the specifications is accepted; turf or running shoes are also acceptable.

front: How many cleats per sole are required, and what is the minimum cleat tip diameter? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 4(i) – Cleat measurements
back: Minimum of 7 cleats per sole, with a minimum cleat tip diameter of 3/16 inch (4.8 mm).

front: What limits apply to additional cleats’ tip diameter and to maximum cleat length? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 4(ii)-(iii) – Cleat size limits
back: Additional cleats may be of lesser tip diameter, provided the maximum length is 1/2 inch (12.7 mm). Maximum cleat length is 1/2 inch (12.7 mm).

front: Which type of cleat is illegal here? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 4(iv) – Illegal cleats
back: A cleat made of metal or with a metal tip is illegal.

front: What is the penalty and game action if a player is using illegal footwear? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 4 Penalty
back: L5 from the point where the ball would have been put into play if no other foul had occurred (or added to the penalty for any other foul). If more than 1 player offends on the same play, only 1 L5 is applied for that play. The offending player shall be removed until the illegal equipment is replaced; immediate substitution will be made, but the game shall not be delayed.

front: What must the head coach (or designated representative) certify to the umpire before the game? Rule 1 | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 5 – Coach’s certification
back: That all players: (a) have been informed of mandatory equipment and what is illegal, (b) have been provided mandatory equipment, (c) have been instructed how to wear the mandatory equipment during the game, and (d) have been instructed to notify the coaching staff when equipment becomes illegal during the game.

front: What must teams do with regard to player registration before the start of the game? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 1 – Registration
back: All players must be registered by name and number with the scorer prior to the start of the game.

front: What is the consequence for an offending player who is not properly registered before the start of the game? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 1 – Registration
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the score sheet has been corrected. Immediate substitution will be made, but the game shall not be delayed.

front: Under what condition is a score by a non-registered player still legal? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 1 – Registration
back: Any score made by a non-registered player is legal, provided the player is then registered on the score sheet.

front: When may substitutes enter the field of play? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: Substitutes may enter the field of play when the ball is dead and only at that time.

front: Where must a player leaving the game go, in order? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: The player leaving the game shall proceed directly to the sideline on which their bench is located, and then to the team bench in the out-of-bounds area.

front: Who controls substitutes, and what limit do they enforce after Team A breaks its huddle? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: The sideline officials (Down Judge and Line Judge) shall control the substitutes. As soon as possible after the ball is dead on a play, they observe their sidelines for possible substitutes until Team A breaks its huddle; then they raise their arms to shoulder level, after which no substitute shall enter the field for any reason—regardless of the number of players a team may have on the field.

front: What makes a substitution proceeding intended to deceive the opponent illegal? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: The use of substitution proceedings, or alleged substitution proceedings to deceive the opponent is illegal.

front: What is a “sleeper play,” and when is it illegal? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: A “sleeper play” is defined as a pass play or kick play designed to deceive the opponent. It is illegal on the subsequent play if one or more Team A players or substitutes legally enter the field or leave the field.

front: In the definition of a sleeper play, what remote-player behavior is described? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: It occurs when an A player remains at the sideline adjacent to their team bench area; often with the ball on the opposite side of the field, Team A lines up quickly, snaps the ball, and throws a forward pass or lateral to a remote A player.

front: What plays are considered legal alternatives to a sleeper play in the rule’s definition? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: A running play, a pass play or kick play to another eligible A player, not in a remote area near their team bench sideline, is legal.

front: If a substitute enters to the extent they can communicate with a teammate, what must they do for the next play? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: They must remain on the field for the subsequent play.

front: What penalties apply when substitution rules are violated due to illegal substitution proceedings and/or a sleeper play? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: Penalty: Team A 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG – L10 DR, 3D DNG-LB, PBD.

front: What penalties apply if a substitute fails to remain on the field for the subsequent play after entering enough to communicate? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: Penalty: Team A 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG-L10 DR, 3D DNG-LB PBD. Team B L10.

front: How many players and/or substitutes may a team have on the field during a play? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 3 – Excess Number of Players
back: It is illegal for a team to have more than 12 players and/or substitutes on the field during a play.

front: What is the penalty for having too many players/substitutes on the field? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 3 – Excess Number of Players
back: Penalty: Team A 1.2D-L10 DR, 3D DG-L10 DR, 3D DNG-LB PBD. Team B L10.

front: Who is responsible for fielding the correct number of players? Rule 1 | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 3 – Excess Number of Players
back: Coaches, not officials, are responsible for fielding the correct number of players.

front: During the game, who may legally occupy positions on the sidelines? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: The field officials, the Downbox Official, the Yardstick Officials, the Time Keeper, and the Scorer.

front: What may occupy a team bench area during the game, and what key restriction applies while play is in progress? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: Only substitute players and other authorized non-playing team personnel (coaches, doctors, trainers, and equipment personnel) may occupy it; they must remain in close proximity to their bench and must not encroach on the sidelines or playing field while play is in progress.

front: How far from the sideline must the team bench area be located (minimum and maximum)? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: A minimum of 5 yards (5 metres) and a maximum of 10 yards (10 metres) from the sideline.

front: What are the enclosure marking requirements for the bench area (width and distances from the sideline)? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: The area is enclosed by a line 4 inches (10 cm) wide, located at least 2 yards (2 metres) minimum and 5 yards (5 metres) optimum from the sideline; there is also a line at each end of the bench 5 yards (5 metres) from the end.

front: When may bench occupants leave the enclosed bench area during the game? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: Except during legal substitution proceedings or by express permission of the Referee, occupants must remain within the enclosed area to keep the sideline clear for officials and coaches.

front: What is the penalty for violations related to sideline/bench restrictions described in Article 1? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: L10, no option, from the point where the ball would have been put in play if no foul had occurred.

front: When is a sideline conference between coaches and players legal? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 2 – Time-Out Conferences
back: During an official time out; and also whenever the clock is stopped and a significant time delay occurs (e.g., a measurement, injury, or TV commercial).

front: Under what circumstances is an unauthorized person prohibited from entering or reaching into the field? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: While play is in progress, the person shall not enter or reach into the field and/or interfere with a player of either team or with a loose ball.

front: What happens if an unauthorized person interferes to act to the advantage of the team in possession? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: If it is obvious to the Referee that a score (such as a rouge or safety touch) would have been made, the score is awarded; otherwise L10 PBH.

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person interferes to act to the advantage of the team not in possession? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: If it is obvious to the Referee that a touchdown would have been scored, or if the unauthorized person is a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of the team bench, a touchdown is awarded; otherwise the non-offending team is awarded (1) half the distance to the goal line from PLS or PBD; (2) for illegal interference on a forward pass: Field of Play = half the distance to the goal line from PF; End zone = depending on the offense: against Team A, ball at the 1-yard line (unless a touchdown is awarded); against Team B, ball at the 20-yard line; and (3) 3 downs, regardless of time remaining (with the stated exceptions).

front: What result applies if an unauthorized person touches or kicks a loose ball? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: If it is obvious to the Referee that a score would have been made, the score is awarded. If the person is a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of the team bench, the team penalized is half the distance to their goal line from PF; if the non-offending team was previously in possession or normally expecting to gain possession by receiving a scrimmage kick, it is awarded the ball and 3 additional downs regardless of time remaining (with the stated exceptions). If not associated with a team as described, the play is repeated at PLS, subject to team penalties applied at PLS.

front: What is the consequence if the unauthorized person is a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of a team bench (interference by unauthorized persons)? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: Disqualification from further participation in any capacity.

front: During a stoppage in play for injury (or other reason), what may team personnel do and what must they not do while on the field? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 5 – Injuries
back: Personnel may enter the field with the Referee’s permission to attend to the injured player or bring water; they may not undertake any coaching activities while on the field.

front: Under what condition does the Referee need not permit attendants of both teams to enter the field? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 5 – Injuries
back: When play has stopped for injury to a player of only 1 team.

front: After a stoppage for a player injury or equipment repair, how many plays must that player sit out? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 5 – Injuries
back: At least three plays for an injury, or at least one play for equipment repair.

front: What is the penalty stated for violations related to the injury personnel rules? Rule 1 | Section 13: Non Players | Article 5 – Injuries
back: L10, no option.
